l4_steps.name: Receive OFP computation trigger from schedule
l4_steps.input: Confirmed flight schedule event (STD, flight number, aircraft registration) published by network scheduling system
l4_steps.output: OFP computation job queued in flight planning system with flight parameters loaded
l4_steps.kpi: OFP computation initiated ≥3 hrs before STD; 100% of flights have confirmed OFP before T-90 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Late aircraft swaps or gate changes in Altéa trigger cascading OFP recomputations; absence of real-time webhook integration between Altéa and NAVBLUE forces manual re-triggers, creating a 10–20 min dispatcher workload spike per swap event

l4_steps.name: Extract aircraft type, reg, and ZFW estimate
l4_steps.input: Flight number, STD, aircraft registration, confirmed bookings, preliminary cargo manifest
l4_steps.output: Aircraft type/registration confirmed, preliminary PAX count, planned Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW) estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Preliminary ZFW within ±2% of final ZFW to ensure accurate early fuel computation
l4_steps.pain_point: Early-trigger OFPs (T-12 hr) carry highly uncertain load estimates; late check-in surges force ZFW and fuel recomputation within the T-1 hr window, causing ramp delays and re-fuelling events that average 18 min delay per occurrence

l4_steps.name: Pull upper-wind, weather, and SIGMET data
l4_steps.input: Route waypoints, planned flight levels, estimated departure time
l4_steps.output: Upper-wind grid data (GRIB2), active SIGMETs/AIRMETs, convective forecast and icing outlook along planned route
l4_steps.kpi: Weather data refresh cycle ≤1 hr before STD; SIGMET coverage 100% of planned route corridor
l4_steps.pain_point: GoDirect data ingestion latency vs. real-time MWO (Meteorological Watch Office) SIGMET issuance can leave a 30–45 min gap for fast-moving convective systems; legacy dispatch integrations without automated SIGMET push alerts rely on dispatcher manual polling

l4_steps.name: Compute CI-optimised route — NAVBLUE
l4_steps.input: O&D city pair, aircraft performance model, upper-wind GRIB2 data, airline cost index (CI) policy
l4_steps.output: Optimised ICAO route string, estimated time en route (ETE), planned FL step-climb profile, preliminary trip fuel
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel saving vs. fixed routing ≥1.2% per flight; cost index adherence to fleet policy (CI 20–35 narrow-body); computation time ≤90 sec
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft performance model currency is a persistent risk — NAVBLUE performance database must be synced with aircraft modification records from AMOS; unrecorded winglet upgrades or engine modifications cause model accuracy drift of up to 0.8% fuel burn, skewing fleet-wide efficiency analytics

l4_steps.name: Calculate trip, contingency, alternate, and reserve fuel
l4_steps.input: NAVBLUE trip fuel output, alternate aerodrome distance and forecast, contingency policy (5% or fixed-minute rule), company extra fuel policy
l4_steps.output: Full fuel breakdown: trip fuel, contingency fuel, alternate fuel, final reserve (30-min FAR 121 / ICAO Annex 6), additional company fuel, total fuel order (kg)
l4_steps.kpi: Actual vs. planned fuel burn variance ≤±3%; zero-fuel-on-arrival (ZFOA) rate <0.1% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 91/121 domestic alternate fuel rules differ from ICAO Annex 6 international rules; carriers operating trans-border routes must maintain dual rule-sets in NAVBLUE configuration — version drift during software updates causes compliance risk and has triggered FAA Letter of Investigation (LOI) actions at US carriers

l4_steps.name: Validate fuel order within MTOW and structural limits
l4_steps.input: Total fuel order (kg), ZFW estimate from Altéa, aircraft MTOW for registration and airport elevation/temperature
l4_steps.output: Go/no-go decision for current routing; if MTOW exceeded, payload reduction request issued to Load Control or route adjusted to reduce trip fuel
l4_steps.kpi: MTOW exceedance rate 0% (hard regulatory limit); fuel reduction iteration cycles ≤2 per flight before escalation
l4_steps.pain_point: High summer temperatures (ISA+15°C or above) at hot/high airports (PHX, DEN, LAS) significantly reduce MTOW-limited payload; NAVBLUE does not provide automated MTOW-constrained route re-optimisation — dispatchers perform manual iteration, averaging 4 additional minutes per constrained flight

l4_steps.name: Filter and review NOTAMs for route and aerodromes
l4_steps.input: Route waypoints, departure/destination/alternate ICAO codes, ETD
l4_steps.output: Filtered NOTAM briefing package with operationally significant NOTAMs highlighted; ILS/approach procedure NOTAMs and runway closure NOTAMs flagged for captain attention
l4_steps.kpi: Dispatcher NOTAM review time ≤8 min per flight; Type I/II NOTAM inclusion rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTAM data quality is a persistent industry problem — free-text, unstructured NOTAMs from certain states require manual parsing; Jeppesen Smart NOTAM keyword filtering reduces volume but has suppressed safety-critical items when taxonomy files are not updated after ICAO format revisions (ICAO Doc 8126 Annex 15 transition 2023)

l4_steps.name: Check ATFM flow programmes and special use airspace
l4_steps.system: FAA TFMS (Traffic Flow Management System) / EUROCONTROL CFMU NM
l4_steps.input: Filed route string, ETD, altitude profile, departure airport capacity programme status
l4_steps.output: Active Ground Delay Programmes (GDPs), Ground Stops (GS), Airspace Flow Programmes (AFP) applicable to flight identified; special use airspace (SUA/TFR) conflicts on route assessed
l4_steps.kpi: ATFM programme impact assessment completed ≥2 hr before STD; SUA conflict detection rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA TFMS GDP data is refreshed every 15–30 min; dispatchers using static NAVBLUE routing miss late-issued GDPs and incur unplanned EDCT delays at departure; military SUA activation in the Gulf of Mexico MOA complex is issued with <1 hr notice, invalidating already-filed ATC FPLs

l4_steps.name: Validate route is clear of restrictions and ATFM conflicts
l4_steps.input: NOTAM flags, SUA/TFR overlap results, applicable GDP/AFP programme constraints
l4_steps.output: Route approved or rerouted alternative generated; if rerouted, OFP recomputed from step 2.1
l4_steps.kpi: Reroute rate due to late SUA/flow conflicts <2% of flights; reroute cycle time (detection to new FPL) ≤12 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Military SUA activation notices (NOTAMs for ranges like W-151, W-168 Gulf ops) can arrive within 45 min of ETD, requiring an emergency reroute that bypasses normal NAVBLUE optimisation and may add 80–150 kg fuel burn on affected sectors

l4_steps.name: File ICAO FPL with ATC via SITA AFTN datalink
l4_steps.input: Completed OFP route string, ETD, ICAO equipment suffix, SELCAL code, aircraft registration, crew identifiers
l4_steps.output: ICAO FPL (format per ICAO Doc 4444 PANS-ATM) transmitted to ATC; ACK or CHG response received and logged
l4_steps.kpi: FPL filed ≥60 min before STD (FAR 91.169 / ICAO Annex 2 requirement); FPL acceptance rate (ACK without CHG) ≥94%
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AFTN message queuing during peak traffic windows (0600–0900 hub banks) adds 5–12 min filing latency; rejected FPLs (CHG messages) require manual field correction and re-filing, consuming 8–15 min of dispatcher time and compressing the pre-departure preparation window

l4_steps.name: Assess EDCT/CTOT slot assignment from ATFM authority
l4_steps.system: FAA TFMS / EUROCONTROL CFMU NM Portal
l4_steps.input: Filed FPL, active GDP/AFP programme data, departure airport acceptance rate
l4_steps.output: EDCT (Expect Departure Clearance Time) or CTOT issued and recorded; or no-restriction confirmation logged
l4_steps.kpi: EDCT compliance rate ≥98%; average ATFM delay per affected flight <8 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Multiple overlapping GDPs (destination GDP + en-route AFP simultaneously) create conflicting EDCT windows that TFMS cannot always auto-resolve; dispatchers must manually arbitrate priority — a process with no formal FAA guidance, leading to inconsistent outcomes across carriers

l4_steps.name: Negotiate slot relief or reroute via AOC coordination
l4_steps.system: FAA TFMS Flight Schedule Monitor (FSM) + EUROCONTROL CFMU NM Portal
l4_steps.input: Assigned EDCT/CTOT, crew duty time remaining, downstream connection passenger count, slot swap availability
l4_steps.output: Slot swap approval or alternate routing clearance granted; updated ETD recorded on OFP; crew notified via ACARS
l4_steps.kpi: Slot relief request success rate ≥30% of attempts; crew duty limit infringement due to ATFM delay <0.5% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: FSM slot-swap portal requires AOC login and a dedicated coordinator — carriers without 24/7 AOC staffing (regional partners, red-eye operations) accept EDCT passively and absorb avoidable delays averaging 22 min per event

l4_steps.name: Generate and transmit OFP package to crew EFB
l4_steps.input: Finalised OFP, fuel order, NOTAM briefing package, weather package, current ATIS
l4_steps.output: Complete OFP briefing packet transmitted to crew EFB via ACARS datalink; delivery acknowledgement logged
l4_steps.kpi: OFP delivery to EFB ≥T-60 min before STD; datalink transmission success rate ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE and Jeppesen FliteDeck EFB require matching document schema versions; version mismatches between aircraft EFB software (often on a slower certification update cycle) and NAVBLUE OFP output format cause rendering failures — crews revert to printed paper fallback, adding 10–15 min to pre-departure preparation

l4_steps.name: Captain reviews OFP fuel, route, and alternates on EFB
l4_steps.input: OFP package including fuel breakdown, route, alternates, NOTAM briefing, weather charts
l4_steps.output: Captain review complete; fuel acceptance confirmed or additional fuel request raised with dispatcher
l4_steps.kpi: Captain OFP review time ≤15 min; OFP acceptance without fuel change ≥82% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Captains on specific high-variability route segments (mountain wave, oceanic NAT) routinely add conservative discretionary fuel above company minima due to low confidence in NAVBLUE model accuracy on those segments — creates 0.3–0.8% fuel burn inefficiency per sector and can push TOW toward MTOW limits on weight-critical flights

l4_steps.name: Resolve captain commander's discretion fuel request
l4_steps.input: Captain's discretionary fuel request (kg), current planned fuel breakdown, MTOW headroom, ramp fuel availability
l4_steps.output: Agreed final fuel quantity; revised fuel order transmitted to ramp fuelling team; updated TOW confirmed within MTOW
l4_steps.kpi: Commander's discretion fuel (CDF) additions >200 kg rate <18% of flights; MTOW exceedance from CDF uplift 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: No structured data capture of CDF rationale in NAVBLUE or FliteDeck — inability to retrospectively analyse CDF patterns by route, captain, or weather condition prevents fuel policy refinement and limits regulatory evidence-gathering under ICAO Annex 6 / EU-OPS ORO.MLR.101 fuel documentation requirements

l4_steps.name: Monitor en-route fuel burn via ACARS position reports
l4_steps.input: ACARS ADS-C/ADS-B position reports with fuel on board (FOB) transmission, OFP fuel plan profile
l4_steps.output: Real-time fuel burn comparison vs. OFP plan; trend line for fuel state at destination and alternate
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel monitoring update interval ≤15 min oceanic / ≤5 min domestic; fuel deviation alert threshold ±5% of plan
l4_steps.pain_point: ADS-C oceanic position reports over HF/SATCOM on North Atlantic and Pacific tracks have 10–30 min latency; dispatchers cannot confirm fuel state in real time for ETOPS critical fuel scenarios and rely on crew self-reporting — a single-point-of-failure monitoring model that increases diversion initiation latency when fuel deviation occurs

l4_steps.name: Assess fuel deviation and issue diversion recommendation
l4_steps.input: ACARS FOB report, computed fuel remaining from OFP, alternate fuel requirement, destination weather update
l4_steps.output: Continue-as-planned confirmation or fuel advisory message to crew; diversion recommendation issued if destination fuel falls below alternate + final reserve requirement
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel emergency declaration rate (MAYDAY FUEL / PAN PAN FUEL) <0.01% of flights; diversion for fuel exhaustion <0.05% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatcher authority to recommend diversion is legally advisory-only under FAR 121.533; PIC has final authority, but late-stage diversions after dispatcher flags critical fuel state incur $40K–$120K IROPS cost per event — absence of a shared decision-making protocol between crew and dispatcher increases initiation latency by an average of 8 min

l4_steps.name: Close flight plan and record actuals in data lake
l4_steps.system: NAVBLUE + Amadeus Altéa PSS + AWS Redshift
l4_steps.input: ACARS actual time of arrival (ATA), final fuel on board at blocks-on, en-route amendment log, uplift confirmation
l4_steps.output: Flight plan closed with ATC; actual fuel burn, block time, and route deviations recorded in airline data lake for performance analytics
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan closure within 30 min of ATA (ICAO Doc 4444 requirement); fuel burn data capture rate 100% for post-flight analytics
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE actuals data is not natively streamed to the airline data lake; a manual export or scheduled ETL pipeline introduces 4–12 hr latency before actuals reach AWS Redshift — preventing same-day fuel efficiency feedback loops and delaying monthly CORSIA fuel reporting submissions
